subject: TCO follow-up: FinPay evaluation vs Hyperscaler / next tests
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa@finpay.com>, Tom Rogers <tom.rogers@cloudvendor.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & TCO summary from today's call (FinPay)

Hi Lisa / Tom —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our end and proposed next steps so we can get the POC scoped: 

Call highlights / assumptions we captured:
- Primary goals: reduce inference unit cost for customer-facing LLM features (multi-turn chat and summarization) and keep 95th p99 latency <= 250ms for common flows.
- Current stack: FinPay running inference on Hyperscaler managed endpoints (Tom confirmed Vertex/SageMaker mix) with model family ~7B–13B for production.
- Main concerns: raw per-1M token cost, unpredictable scaling costs during spikes, and need for SOC2 + KMS for payments data.

High-level TCO comparison (ballpark, per-1M generated + context tokens):
- Redwood (hosted, optimized runtime, 16-batch median, 75% cache hit assumed): ~$3.40 per 1M tokens nominal; effective cost with caching ~ $0.85 per 1M tokens.
- Hyperscaler managed endpoints (current): ~$11–13 per 1M tokens (no prefix KV cache, conservative batching, regional egress and managed infra premium).
- Open-source self-hosted (raw infra only, similar model): ~$5–7 per 1M tokens but requires ops engineering to reach production SLAs.

Key levers we highlighted that drive the delta:
- Prefix/KV caching (we measure cache hit as % of party tokens that skip compute) — 50–80% hit rate typical for chat UIs with repetitive system prompts.
- Batching & dynamic kernels — continuous batching reduces per-token GPU utilization for many workloads (~20–40% saving depending on occupancy).
- Quantization & model variant selection — int8/int4 variants can reduce GPU cost 20–40% for similar quality at certain latency targets.

Proposed next tests / mutual action plan:
1) FinPay sends representative prompt set (10k total prompts covering short/long flows) + sample traffic distribution (token histogram).
2) Redwood runs a 72-hour cost/latency run on a dedicated test pool (we'll provide detailed cost breakdown and per-route latency percentiles).
3) Measure cache hit rates and try two config knobs: (A) prefix cache only, (B) prefix + KV with streaming enabled.
4) Run an integration latency test with 100 concurrent sessions to validate 95th/99th SLOs.

Deliverables from Redwood for the POC:
- Pricing workbook (attached) with per-1M token compute, infra, and support line items.
- SOC2 Type II summary and KMS integration notes (attached).
- Mutual action plan doc and proposed schedule (we'll share a DocuSign + PO-ready invoice template if you want procurement to review).

Next immediate ask from FinPay: can you share the 10k prompt set + token histogram by EOD Wednesday your time? Once we have that we can schedule the POC kickoff (we're available Wed morning or Thu afternoon PST).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow if anything above is unclear.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | (415) 555-0114

From: Lisa Chen <lisa@finpay.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up & TCO summary from today's call (FinPay)

Thanks Aditya — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying questions before we hand the prompt set to procurement: 

1) Can you share the exact assumptions behind the per-1M numbers (especially the cache hit assumption and batching)? We need a line-item breakdown that our finance team can understand (compute vs infra vs data transfer vs support).
2) For the 72-hour run, will you isolate network egress costs separately? Our traffic pattern is multi-region and egress can be material.
3) Any specific format you want the prompt set in? We'll export from our staging logs but want to make sure tokens are counted consistently.

Also please attach the SOC2 doc and the invoice template for procurement to review. If we can get those by tomorrow we can schedule the kickoff for Thu 22 Jul 10:00am PST.

Thanks,
Lisa
Head of Product Integrations | FinPay
lisa@finpay.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa@finpay.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & TCO summary from today's call (FinPay)

Lisa — quick answers to help procurement: 

Assumptions / line-item breakdown (per-1M tokens nominal):
- GPU compute (after model pruning/quant): $2.85
- Serving infra (orchestration, autoscaling, per-request overhead): $0.35
- Network & egress (regional avg): $0.15
- Support & managed services (POC/Onboarding amortized): $0.05
= Total nominal: $3.40 per 1M tokens

Effective cost with caching / batching (example scenario):
- Cache hit 75% -> 75% of tokens skip GPU compute, pay only infra/support/egress on those -> effective compute cost falls to $0.71 per 1M tokens.
- Additional batching/occupancy improvements: we typically observe 20–30% additional reduction on average for chat-style workloads.

72-hour run notes:
- We'll surface a detailed CSV with per-request tokens, observed cache-hit, per-request latency p50/p95/p99, and a cost breakdown CSV (compute vs infra vs egress).
- Egress will be broken out separately in that report.

Prompt set format: a CSV with columns: request_id, role (user/system), prompt_text, expected_tokens_estimate, and a zip of raw request/response examples. Token counting: we'll use the tiktoken-like tokenization we discussed; if you run into mismatches we can run a shared small sanity sample and reconcile.

We'll attach the SOC2 summary and invoice template in this thread (see attachments). Looking forward to kickoff on Thu 22 Jul 10:00am PST — we'll send a calendar invite when you confirm.

—Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
